features.title: Add automatic historical backfill
features.user_visible_behavior: A new account can eventually mirror older messages beyond WINDOW_DAYS without manual intervention while fresh mail stays current.
features.evidence: Revalidated all 7 acceptance criteria against the code on 2026-06-05 (adversarial multi-agent pass). The three-lane engine (ADR 0012) already met criteria 1-5: backfill is on by the schema default historical_backfill_mode='metadata_and_bodies', the hot->body->history lane order keeps fresh mail ahead, historical messages use the same imap_messages/_bodies/_attachments path, and reconcile is window-guarded (window_status='IN_WINDOW') so out-of-window rows are never tombstoned as provider-deleted. The remaining gap was criterion 6 (test coverage) plus a criterion 7 doc nit, both closed in PR #20: integration Scenarios N (multi-cycle batching + resume-from-watermark, no re-snapshot), O (idempotency: re-walking mirrored UIDs upserts with no duplicate rows), P (UIDVALIDITY reset mid-backfill tombstones old-validity rows, clears the stale watermark, and re-mirrors 3/3 cleanly under the new validity), and Q (a fresh account backfills on default settings with no manual config). Verified by pnpm test:db:live (118 spec passes, 4 new scenarios green), pnpm typecheck, pnpm test, pnpm build.
features.notes: Revalidated and completed on 2026-06-05; closed as passing with fresh evidence (PR #20), satisfying the 2026-05-29 maintainer requirement to revalidate rather than infer completion from historical notes. Caveat recorded for future work: criterion 1's 'without manual intervention' holds under normal IMAP conditions; a pathological run of UIDVALIDITY resets (> MAX_UIDVALIDITY_RESETS_24H) still escalates an account to BROKEN like any sync, requiring operator action. Possible future follow-up (not blocking): the history lane currently surfaces its errors into the sync run outcome (can mark an otherwise-healthy account partial_success/DEGRADED); a maintainer decision could isolate history-lane errors from account health to match the 'history completeness does not gate health' intent.

features.title: Add MCP server for AI email tools
features.user_visible_behavior: A local stdio MCP server can safely expose read-oriented mailbox tools against an existing SupaMail database.
features.notes: Per ADR 0014, the MCP server is built in this core repo as a read-only surface; cloud only hosts it. Core owns the server implementation, the read-tool contract, and the local stdio binding; the remote transport, bearer/tenant auth, and MCP token secrets live in supamail-cloud. Build the server with an injected database connection and a transport boundary so the same tool logic runs locally (stdio) and hosted (remote-authed). Start local stdio first; remote transport must be absent from the public package. V1 is read-only. PARTIAL: the read-tool contract for the flagship search tool already exists on branch fedster99/search-layer (ADR 0015) as `search_email` -- apps/api/src/search/mcp-tool.ts exports searchEmailToolDefinition (name/description/inputSchema/readOnlyHint annotations) and runSearchTool(pool, args), both wrapping the same injected-connection searchMessages as the CLI. Remaining for #4: the stdio MCP server process that registers this tool and binds the transport. Do not self-start; this stays not_started until selected.

features.title: Build an agent-first email CLI
features.user_visible_behavior: A local coding agent can inspect mirrored email through stable CLI commands with deterministic, machine-readable output and clear sync trust signals.
features.evidence: Search read layer landed on branch fedster99/search-layer (ADR 0015), the flagship read tool for this CLI. 0007_search_layer.sql adds weighted FTS generated columns + pg_trgm + structured b-tree indexes; apps/api/src/search/ exposes the injected-connection searchMessages function (parser -> SQL compiler -> read-only transaction), a deterministic machine-readable SearchResponse, and a sync_trust block (the sync-trust signal). The `supamail search` CLI command wraps it with JSON output and the full operator/flag surface. Verified 2026-06-07: pnpm typecheck, pnpm test (160 passed incl. 15 parser/compiler unit tests), pnpm build, pnpm test:db:live (migration applied twice for idempotence + src/__tests__/search.live-db.test.ts proving generated columns populate, soft-deletes never leak, a >128KB body does not error, ranking order, and is:/from: operators; 118/118 spec-conformance).
features.notes: Per ADR 0014, the agent CLI is built in this core repo as a read-only surface; cloud only hosts it (build location is not run location). The search command is the first read command and shares the read-tool contract with issue #4. Remaining for #7: additional read commands (e.g. get-message, thread view) and a non-JSON pretty mode. Sending, scheduling, contacts, calendar, CRM hydration, and AI summarization stay out of scope unless a later ADR explicitly adds them. WIP=1: do not start a second feature while this is in_progress.
